title: Optimization config rollback edge cases (runtime): KV cache, continuous batching, quantization swaps, warmup
author: Omar El-Sayed
body:
## Summary
This page documents known runtime edge cases when applying or rolling back Optimize configuration (batching, caching, and quantization profile knobs). The goal is to keep rollback safe under pressure (on-call use) and avoid split-brain behavior while preserving correctness.

This is **not** a full design doc; it is a pragmatic reference for runtime + SRE responders and for the preflight validator/guardrails.

## Scope / assumptions
Applies to:
- Hosted API, Dedicated clusters, and Private deployments using the Redwood serving runtime.
- Rollback semantics for the **whole config** at a given scope (route/model/customer/cluster), as implemented by the Safe apply + rollback mechanism.

Assumptions:
- Config apply/rollback is **atomic per scope** (single effective version at any time per scope).
- Runtime uses a **lease/lock** to prevent concurrent applies/rollbacks for the same scope.
- Runtime reports propagation status back to the control plane (for progress UI and auditability).

## Why rollbacks are tricky in the runtime
Rollback is logically “set config back to version N”, but the runtime has state that may outlive a config flip:
- KV caches and prefix caches may contain data computed under a different schedule/precision.
- Continuous batching and scheduler queues may have in-flight requests using the previous config.
- Quantization profile changes affect weights/activation kernels and sometimes memory layout.
- Warmup behavior (graph compilation, kernel autotune, paged KV allocator state) can cause temporary latency spikes or OOM if not handled.

This page enumerates known failure modes and the expected/approved mitigations.

---

## Recommended safe defaults (when in doubt)
These defaults are intended for *rollback targets* and for “safety-mode” fallbacks when the runtime detects a risky transition.

**Table: Safety defaults (per model/route unless stated otherwise)**
- Batching:
  - max_batch_size_tokens: 8192 (Hosted), 16384 (Dedicated), 8192 (Private default unless sized)
  - max_concurrent_sequences: 32
  - continuous_batching: enabled
  - queue_wait_ms (max): 10ms
- Caching:
  - kv_cache: enabled
  - prefix_cache: enabled (if supported by model), but **invalidate on rollback across quantization changes**
  - kv_cache_eviction: LRU, target_utilization <= 0.85
- Quantization:
  - default quant_profile: "fp16" (or "bf16" where supported)
  - disallow rollback target that mixes quant profiles across shards (see edge case Q4)
- Warmup:
  - warmup_on_apply: enabled
  - warmup_concurrency: 1 per worker
  - warmup_max_tokens: 256 prompt + 64 decode

Notes:
- “Bigger batch” is not always safer. The numbers above aim to avoid OOM on common GPU shapes and reduce tail latency risk.
- Dedicated/Private may tune higher, but rollback targets should favor stability.

---

## Edge cases and mitigations

### KV cache + prefix cache interactions

#### K1: Rolling back changes that alter KV cache layout/precision
**Symptoms**
- Increased error rate immediately after rollback (e.g., CUDA illegal memory access, shape mismatch)
- Rare correctness issues if cached tensors are interpreted under a different dtype/layout

**Typical triggers**
- Switching quantization profile (fp16 <-> int8/fp8)
- Toggling paged KV allocator modes (if exposed)
- Changing attention kernel selection mode in a way that changes KV packing

**Mitigation (runtime behavior)**
- On config transitions where the runtime detects a KV layout/precision incompatibility, it must:
  1) **Invalidate KV + prefix caches** for the affected scope (route/model shard set).
  2) Drain in-flight requests (see batching section) before accepting new requests under the new config.

**Mitigation (operator guidance)**
- Expect a short-lived latency increase due to cold caches.
- Prefer rollback targets that keep the same quantization profile when the incident is not quant-related.

**Guardrail (preflight validator)**
- Mark as WARNING if rollback crosses quant profile boundary; require acknowledgement in Console.
- Mark as ERROR if rollback attempts “mixed mode” across shards (see Q4).


#### K2: Cache poisoning across routing changes
**Symptoms**
- Elevated tail latency, uneven GPU utilization
- Increased cache miss rate / prefix cache churn

**Typical triggers**
- Rollback changes smart routing policy that shifts traffic across regions or GPU pools without coordinated cache behavior

**Mitigation**
- Treat routing rollback as a traffic-shape change; use canary apply if possible.
- Ensure cache namespaces include scope versioning where applicable (prefix cache keys should include model_id + tokenizer_version + quant_profile + relevant decoding knobs).

**Operational note**
- In Hosted, routing policies can shift traffic across shared pools; cache effects are amplified.


### Continuous batching + scheduler state

#### B1: In-flight request mixing during rollback
**Symptoms**
- Latency spikes or intermittent timeouts during rollback
- “Stuck” sequences in the scheduler (rare) when queue policies change mid-flight

**Typical triggers**
- Rolling back max_concurrent_sequences, queue_wait_ms, or batching aggressiveness
- Rolling back speculative decoding / draft model settings (if enabled)

**Mitigation (runtime behavior)**
- Rollback should be applied with a two-phase approach per worker:
  1) **Freeze admission** for new requests for the affected scope.
  2) Allow in-flight sequences to finish OR time-box and fail fast with retryable errors (policy-driven).
  3) Apply config + reset scheduler parameters.
  4) Resume admission.

**Recommended time-box**
- Hosted: 30s max drain before fail-fast
- Dedicated/Private: 60–120s max drain (customers often prefer fewer retries)

**Guardrail**
- If queue_wait_ms decreases materially (e.g., >50% reduction), warn that throughput may drop and p95 may improve; if it increases materially, warn about tail latency.


#### B2: Rollback to more aggressive batching causing OOM
**Symptoms**
- OOMs shortly after rollback, typically on long-context prompts
- GPU resets / worker restarts

**Typical triggers**
- Rolling back from conservative max_batch_size_tokens to a higher value
- Rolling back from smaller kv_cache_target_utilization to larger (less headroom)

**Mitigation**
- Runtime should clamp to safe bounds (service-level caps) even if config requests higher.
- If an OOM occurs within N minutes after rollback, the runtime should surface a specific propagation failure reason including the clamp values and observed max context.

**Guardrail (default caps)**
- Enforce max_batch_size_tokens hard cap per GPU type/worker memory budget.
- Enforce kv_cache_target_utilization <= 0.90 hard cap.


### Quantization profile swaps

#### Q1: Rollback crosses quant profile boundary (int8/fp8 <-> fp16/bf16)
**Symptoms**
- Warmup latency spike (kernel compilation / autotune)
- Temporary throughput drop due to weight re-load
- Elevated error rate if weights not available locally or download is slow (Private)

**Mitigation (runtime behavior)**
- Treat quant-profile boundary crossing as a “restart-like” transition for the model shard:
  - Explicitly reload weights into the correct format.
  - Invalidate caches (KV + prefix) as per K1.
  - Run a bounded warmup.

**Mitigation (operator guidance)**
- Prefer canary apply for quant profile rollbacks on high-traffic routes.
- In Private/air-gapped deployments, ensure the target quant artifacts exist on disk before initiating rollback.


#### Q2: Rollback to a quant profile that is incompatible with current driver/kernel set
**Symptoms**
- Apply/rollback fails in preflight (best case) or during runtime warmup (worst case)

**Typical triggers**
- Private deployments with older NVIDIA driver/CUDA
- Worker image drift

**Mitigation**
- Preflight must validate quant profile compatibility against the cluster’s runtime capabilities (driver, compute capability, kernel bundle versions).
- Runtime must produce explicit errors with remediation (upgrade driver/image or select a compatible quant profile).


#### Q3: Silent quality change after rollback
**Symptoms**
- No infra errors, but customer reports output quality regression

**Typical triggers**
- Rolling back quant profile that changes numeric behavior (fp8 vs fp16)
- Rolling back decoding knobs indirectly tied to quant recommendation

**Mitigation**
- Treat this as an expected risk; this project’s initial release is not fully automatic quality rollback.
- If available, run post-apply eval signals (shadow prompts) as metric gates in canary.

**Recommended operator response**
- If incident is customer-facing quality: rollback again to last known-good version with matching quant profile, then engage Applied ML/Optimize to re-validate.


#### Q4: Mixed quant profile across shards / partial propagation
**Symptoms**
- Inconsistent behavior across requests, hard-to-debug error patterns

**Why it happens**
- Apply/rollback attempted while some workers are unavailable; some shards move forward, others stay behind.

**Mitigation (must-have)**
- Runtime must not serve mixed quant profiles for the same model scope. If a quant profile change cannot be applied to all required shards in the scope, the runtime should:
  - Fail the apply/rollback operation and keep the previous effective version, OR
  - Enter a safe “serve previous version only” mode while retrying propagation (policy depends on environment).

**Operator guidance**
- If Console shows partial propagation on rollback: do not retry rapidly. Follow the rollback runbook escalation path to address unhealthy workers first.

---

## Warmup behavior and rollout safety

### W1: Warmup-induced latency spike after rollback
**Symptoms**
- p95 latency increases immediately after rollback, then recovers

**Root cause**
- Cold caches + kernel selection/autotune + weight reload

**Mitigation**
- Warmup must be **bounded** and **serialized per worker** to avoid GPU thrash.
- Warmup traffic should be tagged (trace attribute + metrics label) to keep SLO dashboards interpretable.

**Suggested warmup recipe**
- 3 iterations of a small prompt/decode pair (256/64) per shard.
- Ensure warmup does not use customer prompts.


### W2: Warmup causing OOM due to worst-case context
**Symptoms**
- OOM during warmup, especially if warmup uses a too-large prompt length

**Mitigation**
- Warmup must be conservative and not exceed configured max_context for the route/model.
- Prefer a small fixed warmup token count rather than sampling production distribution.

---

## Known operational pitfalls (for SRE/on-call)
1) **Rollback succeeded but latency did not recover**
   - Check cache invalidation occurred (KV/prefix). If not, suspect K1/K2 behavior.
   - Check if rollback crossed quant boundary and caused cold start.
   - Verify admission control drained properly (B1).

2) **Rollback action keeps failing with “propagation incomplete”**
   - Likely unhealthy workers or capacity constraints. Resolve worker health first.
   - Avoid repeated rollbacks; each attempt may churn caches and worsen impact.

3) **Dedicated tenant: rollback appears to work but only some traffic improves**
   - Investigate traffic splitting/routing policy. Confirm scope correctness (route vs model vs customer).

4) **Private deployments: rollback is slow**
   - Weight artifacts may be missing locally; verify artifact availability.
   - Check disk throughput constraints; quant swap can be IO-heavy.

---

## What the runtime must log/emit (to make this debuggable)
For every apply/rollback attempt, runtime should emit:
- config_scope_id, target_version_id, previous_version_id
- correlation_id / request_id (from control plane)
- phase timing: drain_start/end, cache_invalidate_start/end, weight_reload_start/end, warmup_start/end
- result: success | failed | partial (partial should be treated as failure for quant swaps)
- failure_reason enum (e.g., WORKER_UNHEALTHY, OOM, QUANT_INCOMPATIBLE, LOCK_TIMEOUT)

Metrics (high-level)
- config_apply_duration_seconds{scope, result}
- config_rollback_duration_seconds{scope, result}
- config_propagation_stuck{scope}
- cache_invalidation_count{scope, cache_type}
- warmup_duration_seconds{model, quant_profile}

---

## Appendix A: Quick edge-case matrix
- KV cache + quant swap: invalidate caches + reload weights + bounded warmup
- Batching knob rollback: freeze admission + drain + apply + resume
- Aggressive batching rollback: clamp + warn; canary where possible
- Partial propagation: never allow mixed quant; fail or serve previous version only

## Appendix B: Open questions / follow-ups
1) Define the exact “serve previous version only while retrying propagation” policy per environment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) Confirm cache keying includes all knobs that influence numerical outputs (quant_profile, attention kernel family, tokenizer/version).
3) Decide whether to offer an operator-toggle for “drain with fail-fast” vs “drain to completion” in rollback UI (default per environment).

Changelog
- 2025-02-21: Added explicit prohibition on mixed quant profile across shards (Q4) and clarified warmup recipe bounds.
- 2025-02-03: Expanded scheduler drain time-box defaults and added guardrails for batching OOM scenarios.
- 2025-01-14: Initial publication.
